engine_versions_provenance: read from the local binaries with `-v`; the gitignored prebuild cache is consulted only as a cross-check and is not required
resources_provenance: Pinned by GitHub release-asset ID. meta-rules-dat publishes only a rolling `latest` release with no dated tag, so download/latest/... points at whatever was rebuilt most recently and changes without notice. An asset ID names one immutable upload.
resources_release: Release 2026-11-02 01:42 (repinned twice on 2026-11-02: the 2026-10-28 and 2026-11-01 releases were both deleted upstream within the hour)

verge-mihomo.why: Committed bytes, fetched from the commit-pinned raw URL. A stable GitHub release asset is the more durable upstream, but it is still an upstream: the build must not depend on one being reachable.

verge-mihomo-alpha.why: MetaCubeX publishes the mihomo alpha as a single rolling prerelease and deletes older builds, so its download URL stops existing, and a *single* vendored platform converted the 3.3.4 outage into a single-platform build. All four triples are vendored.

clash-verge-service.why: The privileged helper the client installs. Its upstream is stable, so this is not an outage measure: without it a fresh clone cannot verify every pin it holds, and `--check` reports these three as MISSING before prebuild has ever run — a check that fails on a correct tree, which is how a check stops being read.

resources.why: meta-rules-dat republished on 2026-10-28 and the previously pinned asset IDs 404'd, stopping the 3.3.4 build. An asset ID names one immutable upload but not a permanent one; the bytes that passed their pin are the ones worth keeping.

what: The build inputs prebuild.mjs downloads, pinned by sha256 of the bytes actually used. See server/scripts/sidecar-lock.py.
